Combine the two source documents below into one merged document that carries
every fact from both.

Rules:
- Every fact stated in either source must appear in the merge. A fact that is
  dropped cannot be recovered later, so this is the failure that matters most.
- Nothing may appear in the merge that neither source states. Do not add
  context, do not fill gaps from your own knowledge, do not infer a fact from
  two others.
- A fact both sources state is stated once, not twice.
- Where the two sources give different values for the same attribute, state
  both values, name the document each one came from, and do not choose between
  them. Say that the sources disagree. Never pick a winner and never average,
  reconcile or split the difference.
- Never attribute a fact to a document that does not state it. Attribute a
  value only when you are surfacing a disagreement, and then only to the
  document that value actually came from.
- Copy values, names, numbers, units, dates and time formats character for
  character. Do not normalise, round, expand or abbreviate them. "approximately
  500" stays "approximately 500"; "07:15 till 19:45" stays "07:15 till 19:45".
  Copy any spelling, grammatical or formatting error exactly as it stands; do
  not correct anything.
- Order, headings and wording are yours to choose. Reorganise, retitle and
  rewrite as freely as you like. The merge is not graded on prose, only on
  whether every fact survived it unchanged.

Worked example - one attribute, two values.

Suppose the two sources were:

  marlbrook_handbook.md
    The Marlbrook funicular climbs 412 metres.
    The cars run every 20 minutes.

  marlbrook_field_notes.md
    The Marlbrook funicular climbs 412 metres.
    The cars run every 15 minutes.
    The lower station has a ticket office.

Then the merged document is:

  The Marlbrook funicular climbs 412 metres.

  Unresolved: the interval between cars.
  marlbrook_handbook.md states that the cars run every 20 minutes.
  marlbrook_field_notes.md states that the cars run every 15 minutes.
  The sources disagree and this merge does not choose between them.

  The lower station has a ticket office.

The climb appears once, because both sources state it and they agree. The
interval appears twice, once per document, because they disagree - both values
are kept, each named to the document it came from, and neither is chosen. The
ticket office is stated by one source only, and is carried over unattributed
like any other fact.

This example is an illustration. Nothing from it belongs in your answer unless
the documents below happen to state it.

Return JSON matching the provided schema. Put the entire merged document in
merged_document as a single string. Nothing else.

source_a.md:
# Vandrell Relay — Operator Guide

Vandrell Relay is a fictional HTTP relay. This document is test data.

## Networking

The relay listens on port 8443 by default.
The default connect timeout is 30 seconds.
The default read timeout is 120 seconds.

## Limits

The relay accepts at most 512 concurrent connections.
Each request is retried at most 3 times.

## Security

The minimum accepted TLS version is TLS 1.2.


source_b.md:
# Vandrell Relay — Deployment Notes

Vandrell Relay is a fictional HTTP relay. This document is test data.

## Runtime

The relay listens on port 8443 by default.
The relay accepts at most 512 concurrent connections.
One worker process is started per CPU core.

## Logging

Access logs are written in JSON Lines format.
Log files are rotated when they reach 100 megabytes.

## Health

The health check endpoint is /-/healthy.
A relay that fails 3 consecutive health checks is removed from rotation.
